findings.title: `deleteMany` with top-level `OR` across unindexed `retryCount` causes a full table scan on `WorkflowReminder`
findings.body: In `packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts` (lines 29-45), the `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` query was changed from filtering on `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }` (which is covered by the composite index `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`) to a top-level `OR` whose second branch is `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`. `retryCount` is not indexed on `WorkflowReminder` in `packages/prisma/schema.prisma`, and placing it in a top-level `OR` without `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` forces PostgreSQL to sequentially scan the entire `WorkflowReminder` table (including `EMAIL` and `WHATSAPP` reminders) on every cron invocation. Scoping the `where` clause by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` at the top level and/or indexing `retryCount` (or deleting the reminder directly when `reminder.retryCount >= 1` instead of incrementing and deleting on the next run) avoids scanning the whole table every cron tick.
